```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(plotly)
library(fivethirtyeight)
library(data.table)

candy <- fivethirtyeight::candy_rankings 

candy <- candy |> 
  mutate(type = case_when(
    chocolate & fruity ~ "both",
    chocolate ~ "chocolate",
    fruity ~ "fruity",
    .default = "other"
  ))

```

#Vizualization 1

## Row 1 {height="30%"}

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Total Candies"

list(
  icon = "basket", 
  color = "warning", 
  value = nrow(candy))

```

```{r}

list(

```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox

list(

```

## Row 2

```{r}
boxplot <- ggplot(candy, aes(type, winpercent, color = type, fill = type)) + 
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.15, width = 0.55, outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(y = "Win %",
       x = "Candy Type")

ggplotly(boxplot)
```

```{r}
bar <- ggplot(candy, aes(winpercent, reorder(competitorname, winpercent), fill = type)) +
  geom_col() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 4)) +
  labs(y = "Candy Name",
       x = "Win %")

ggplotly(bar)
```

```{r}
candy <- candy |>
  select(competitorname, sugarpercent, winpercent) |>
  drop_na() |>
  arrange(desc(sugarpercent))

most_sugar <- candy |>
  slice_max(sugarpercent, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

least_sugar <- candy |>
  slice_min(sugarpercent, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

average_popularity <- mean(candy$winpercent)
```

## Overview

#### Research Question

Does more sugar mean more popular?

This dashboard explores the relationship between sugar content and candy popularity using the FiveThirtyEight candy rankings dataset. The scatterplot and regression line will help identify whether candies with higher sugar content tend to receive higher popularity scores.

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Most Sugary Candy"
#| color: danger

list(
  icon = "candy-cane",
  value = most_sugar$competitorname,
  caption = paste0(
    round(most_sugar$sugarpercent * 100, 1),
    "% sugar"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Least Sugary Candy"
#| color: success

list(
  icon = "leaf",
  value = least_sugar$competitorname,
  caption = paste0(
    round(least_sugar$sugarpercent * 100, 1),
    "% sugar"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Average Popularity"
#| color: primary

list(icon = "chart-line", 
     value = paste0(round(average_popularity, 1), "%"),
     caption = "Average candy popularity score")
```

## Sugar vs. Popularity

```{r}
#| title: "Sugar Content vs. Candy Popularity"
#| fig-height: 6

sugar_plot <- ggplot(candy,aes(x = sugarpercent, y = winpercent, 
                               text = paste0("Candy: ", competitorname,
                                             "<br>Sugar: ", round(sugarpercent * 100, 1), 
                                             "%",
                                             "<br>Popularity: ", round(winpercent, 1), "%"))) +
  geom_point(color = "#00B8D9", size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#FF8C42", fill = "#FF8C42", alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(x = "Sugar Percentage", y = "Popularity Score (%)", 
       title = "Does More Sugar Mean More Popular?") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

ggplotly(sugar_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

## Candy Rankings

```{r}
#| title: "Candy Rankings Data"

data.table(candy |>
                dplyr::mutate(sugarpercent = round(sugarpercent * 100, 1),
                              winpercent = round(winpercent, 1)),
              colnames = c("Candy", "Sugar Percentage", "Win Percentage"),
              rownames = FALSE, options = list(
                pageLength = 10,
                searching = TRUE,
                ordering = TRUE,
                scrollX = TRUE))

sugar_correlation <- cor(candy$sugarpercent, candy$winpercent)

sugar_correlation
```
